comparison: Both evaluations strongly support TGN46's role as a cargo receptor for PAUF export via CARTS. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative measurements and statistical support from multiple experimental approaches (secretion assays, microscopy, FLIP). Peer reviewers explicitly affirm this as a 'fundamental insight' and 'significant contribution.' Both agree the evidence is compelling. OpenEval includes C3 and C76 not mentioned in peer evaluation.

Both evaluations support pathway specificity findings showing TGN46 affects PAUF but not VSVG carriers. OpenEval notes the mechanism of selectivity requires further investigation. Peer reviewers accept these findings as part of the 'compelling' data and 'clear model.' OpenEval includes C6 (perinuclear localization) which peer review addresses separately.

Perfect agreement on PKD-KD experiments (C17-C20) demonstrating cargo sorting function distinct from membrane deformation. Both evaluations support the interpretation that unchanged tubule number with reduced PAUF loading provides strong evidence for cargo sorting. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these findings as part of the overall demonstration of TGN46's cargo receptor function.

Complete agreement on cytosolic tail deletion experiments (C29, C31-C37). Both evaluations support that TGN46 loading into CARTS is independent of the cytosolic terminus. OpenEval provides detailed quantitative analysis, while peer reviewers explicitly note this as one of the 'new insights' obtained. Both agree the data support localization role but not CARTS incorporation dependency.

Full agreement on TMD experiments (C42-C48, C50, C54) showing that localization is maintained despite TMD alterations, but CARTS specificity and export kinetics are affected. Both evaluations support the conclusion against hydrophobic matching as primary localization mechanism. Peer reviewers note 'balanced and constructive' presentation of interpretations.

Strong agreement on necessity of luminal domain (C55-C59). Both evaluations emphasize that the luminal domain is 'crucial' for PAUF incorporation into CARTS. OpenEval highlights convergent phenotypes from microscopy and FLIP data. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm the luminal domain's importance for both cargo receptor function and TGN46 localization.

Both evaluations support sufficiency of luminal domain (C60-C70) through gain-of-function experiments. OpenEval emphasizes that soluble TGN46lum maintains function and redirects other cargoes to CARTS. Peer reviewers explicitly note the luminal domain 'contains a positive signal for Golgi export in CARTS.' Both agree these experiments demonstrate sufficiency. OpenEval includes C62, C64, C66 not explicitly mentioned in peer evaluation.

Agreement on kinetic correlation findings (C71-C72, C108-C109). OpenEval notes the modest r² value (~0.4) indicates substantial variability and additional factors beyond CARTS specificity. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these kinetic analyses as part of the 'clear model' and 'significant contribution,' without raising concerns about the correlation strength.

Both evaluations support rescue experiments (C73-C75) demonstrating selective rescue by constructs containing luminal domain. OpenEval notes partial rescue suggests compensatory mechanisms. Peer reviewers accept these data as supporting the proposed model and note 'balanced and constructive' presentation of interpretations.

Perfect agreement on uncertainty regarding C5 (glycosylation speculation). Both evaluations note this is speculative without direct experimental support. OpenEval explicitly states 'no direct glycosylation analysis or enzymatic assays are provided.' Peer reviewers do not challenge but also do not explicitly comment, consistent with viewing this as a minor speculative observation.

OpenEval supports C6 (perinuclear localization in both cell types) based on immunofluorescence microscopy. Peer review groups this with pathway specificity claims (C8-C12) and does not separately evaluate C6, but accepts the overall selectivity findings as 'compelling.'

Both evaluations support IDR characterization (C89-C90) based on PONDR analysis. OpenEval notes experimental validation would strengthen the conclusion. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this characterization as it underlies the biomolecular condensate speculation they acknowledge, without raising concerns about the computational prediction.

Both evaluations mark C94 (TGN46 sorting integrins) as uncertain/speculative. OpenEval explicitly states this 'requires testing with integrin trafficking experiments.' Peer reviewers group this with other speculative proposals (C113-C114) and acknowledge the speculative nature, noting authors present these as hypotheses for future investigation.

Both evaluations identify C113-C114 (ER-Golgi contacts, Cab45 relationship) as explicitly speculative without experimental support. OpenEval notes testing would be needed. Peer reviewers acknowledge 'speculative part of the manuscript' regarding broader mechanistic proposals including biomolecular condensates. Both agree these represent hypotheses rather than established findings.

OpenEval supports C51 (no strong TGN46 oligomerization) based on co-immunoprecipitation data, noting this doesn't rule out weak/transient interactions. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific claim.

OpenEval supports C22-C28, C40-C41, C88 as well-established structural facts about TGN46 from prior literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, likely because these are background information rather than new findings requiring evaluation.

OpenEval supports C30, C77-C87 as established literature providing context and identifying knowledge gaps. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these represent prior knowledge motivating the current work rather than new experimental findings.

OpenEval supports C38-C39, C100-C104 citing established literature on membrane thickness gradients and TMD-based sorting mechanisms. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background/contextual claims.

OpenEval supports C95-C99 as established prior literature on TGN46 interactions and functions providing context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these are background citations rather than new experimental claims.

OpenEval supports C105-C107, noting agreement between current TMD results and prior modeling/experimental work on Golgi organization. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these summary/contextual claims.

OpenEval supports C16 as established literature describing PKD-KD phenotype, noting appropriate use of this tool. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this methodological background claim.
